input_text: Text: Santa Fe is so far mum on the more than $2 billion stock swap takeover proposal from Newmont, announced Thursday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Wall Street, since the bid, has speculated that any deal between Newmont and Santa Fe would be a "bear hug," or a reluctantly negotiated agreement where the buyer is not necessarily a friendly suitor. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Newmont said the companies have had previous contact, though declined to detail the encounters. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Analysts predict Santa Fe will go to the highest bidder, and that if a rival buyer is found, Newmont may not be able to match its offer. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: They said the Santa Fe deal, which includes desirable Nevada mining territory, would only payoff for Newmont longer term. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Newmont, in fact, will not benefit from the Santa Fe acquisition on an earnings basis for at least two years, which also limits its capacity to raise its offer. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Any deal, friendly or hostile, would almost assuredly be a stock swap, which is necessary to preserve the tax-free, pooling-of-interest accounting, they said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Analysts and arbitrageurs immediately ruled out Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd as Santa Fe saviors because they are locked in negotiations over their splitting Indonesia's Busang vast gold deposit. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Placer Dome Inc too was considered unlikley because it is focusing on geographic expansion in areas that do match Santa Fe's Nevada, South America and Central Asia presence, they said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: A Homestake spokesman was not immediately available to comment on speculation that it tops the list. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Homestake, based in San Francisco, operates gold mines in the United States, Australia, Chile and Canada. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Earnings in 1995 were $0.22 per share, or $30.3 million, on revenues of $746.3 million. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Santa Fe is headquartered Albuquerque, N.M. and reported 1995 earnings of $0.30 per share, or $40 million, on revenues of $350 million. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Santa Fe has mining and exploration operations in Nevada, California, Montana, Canada, Brazil, Australia, Chile, Kazakstan, Mexico and Ghana. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: PaineWebber analyst Marc Cohen said he lowered his rating on Newmont to neutral from attractive today because if Newmont merged with Santa Fe, investors would have to wait until the second half of 1998 to realize earnings accretion. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "I think Homestake could come in as a white knight, but how much is someone willing to come in above the Newmont number. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: One would have to outbid by at least 15 percent, but there is going to be a (Santa Fe) deal with someone, "he said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "Longer term, two to three years out, (a Newmont-Santa Fe deal) is positive, it does all the right things. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But in the near-term it is, at worst, neutral, "the analyst added. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Newmont proposed to Santa Fe a stock-swap merger at a ratio of 0.33 Newmont shares for each Santa Fe shares. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Plastic surgery gets boost in Brazil. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Simona de Logu Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: RIO DE JANEIRO 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Plastic surgery is booming, especially among men, as Brazilians spend much of their new-found wealth on the latest beauty treatments, said the organisers of a four-day international plastic surgery conference that opened on Friday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The number of plastic surgeries in Brazil has jumped 30 percent to an estimated 150,000 this year since an anti-inflation plan was introduced in July 1994, Farid Hakme, the president of the Brazilian Plastic Surgery Society (SBCP), said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The number of operations on men increased even more -- by 80 percent, from 8,000 in 1994 to 15,000 in 1995, he said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "Brazil ranks right at the top for plastic surgery with respect to the number of surgeons, the number of patients, number of operations, number of conferences. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Our statistics are the highest for everything, "Hakme said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "We believe the increase in plastic surgeries for men results from the difficulties in the job market. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: People need to have a more youthful look to compete in the job market, given the profound changes in Latin America's economy. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: A controlled exchange rate, trade liberalisation and tight monetary policies have also dramatically curbed inflation, making more money available for cosmetic surgery. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Brazil has been at the forefront in plastic surgery for decades and is home to one of the most famous surgeons, Ivo Pitangy. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: There are 6,000 plastic surgeons there, of which 4,500 have qualified to be members of the SBCP. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Every year, 500 new plastic surgeons graduate in Brazil and medical students from all over the world come to study there. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Hakme attributes Brazil's fascination with plastic surgery not to excessive vanity but to the country's mix and match of different races, which can create physical disharmonies. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: What happens is the nose sometimes doesn't match the mouth or the buttocks don't match with the legs, "he said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Brazil's most sought-after beauty treatment is liposuction in which fat is sucked away from areas of the body, with about 30,000 operations a year at a cost of $3,000 to $4,000 each. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Stomach tucks and breast operations are also popular since the tropical climate calls for flesh-baring fashions, but unlike women elsewhere Brazilians tend to have breast reductions and buttock implants. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "The women who want to reduce their breasts here would probably want to increase them in the United States," SBCP Vice-President Oswaldo Saldanha said. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Beauty ideals and cultures are different in every country. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Plastic surgery scares like the case in which Brazilian model Claudia Liz fell into a coma after being anaesthetised for a liposuction in October are not much of a deterrent. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Saldanha said operations fell 30 percent immediately after that case but the rate was back to normal now. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: DILI, East Timor 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: East Timorese Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo left Dili on Friday on his way to Norway for the awards ceremony as co-recipient of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: will exacerbate the problem in finding a solution (to East Timor), "Alatas said on Friday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: He was responding to questions at a news conference called to discuss next week's ministerial meeting of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) in Jakarta. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Ramos Horta has been a vocal leader of the opposition to Jakarta's rule in the territory. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Belo and Ramos Horta were awared the prize for their efforts to secure a peaceful solution to the issue of East Timor, a former Portuguese colony which Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The United Nations has never recognised Jakarta's move. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Japan's authorities seen seeking to rein in dollar. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Comments by Japan's tight-lipped central bank chief and an influential top bureaucrat are further signs that the nation's authorities want to keep the dollar at current levels, market sources said on Friday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Asked about Rubin's comment that a strong dollar was in U.S. interests, Sakakibara said the remark does not necessarily mean the United States supports a stronger dollar. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "It's a strong dollar, not stronger. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: In that sense, the comments are not pointing to a certain direction, "he said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "It shows that Sakakibara is not for a stronger dollar either," said Sumitomo's Note. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Takao Sakoh, first vice president at Union Bank of Switzerland in Tokyo, said: "Maybe a dollar at 104.50 yen is not acceptable (to Sakakibara), but it may be okay at the current level, at the lower end of 112 yen." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Market participants have kept a close eye on Sakakibara, chief of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, as a comment he made in November after the dollar hit this year's high of 114.92 yen pushed the currency down sharply. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "The recent level of the yen exchange rate has been stable, and it does not appear to be moving towards a further depreciation of the yen immediately, so import prices are likely to stabilise at current levels," Matsushita said in an interview with the Nihon Keizai Shimbun. Text: 14 years later, Florida man dies for killing. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Fourteen years after he bludgeoned and shot a man whose trailer home he robbed in 1982, John Mills Jr. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: , 41, was put to death in Florida's electric chair Friday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: As Glenn Lawhon, a rural Florida minister who is the victim's father, looked on, Mills was pronounced dead at 7:13 a.m. EST (1213 GMT) for the murder of Lester Lawhon. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Speaking in Arabic, Mills made a final statement before an anonymous citizen flipped the switch that sent 2000 volts of electricity through his body, said Department of Corrections spokesman Eugene Morris, who was present at the execution. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "I bear witness that there is no God but Allah and I bear witness that the prophet Mohammed is the messenger of God," he quoted Mills as saying. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Prison officials said they had no record of Mills' official conversion, but they said that, on May 14, 1991, he had asked that a new name, Yuhanna Abdullah Muhammed, be added to his prison file, which is usually an indication of a conversion to Islam. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Mills is the 38th person to die in Florida's electric chair since the U.S. Supreme Court reversed itself in 1976 and legalised the death penalty. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Prison officials said Mills made no special request for a last meal and did not eat the steak, fried potatoes and orange juice offered him. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: He spent Thursday with family members and his spiritual adviser, Morris said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Mills was scheduled to die Wednesday but had his sentence temporarily postponed by the Florida Supreme Court. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: On Thursday, the 11th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in Atlanta denied his appeal in federal court. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: In March 1982, Mills and accomplice Michael Frederick knocked on the door of Lester Lawhon's trailer in an attempt to rob it, police said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Lester Lawhon was taken to a nearby airstrip where he was bludgeoned with a tire iron. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Mills then fired two shots that killed Lawhon as the victim tried to run away. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Frederick is serving a 347-year sentence. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "But there are a lot of dinosaurs here. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Bre-X, Barrick said to continue Busang talks. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: K.T. Arasu Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: JAKARTA 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp are to continue negotiations to hammer out a partnership agreement to develop the spectacular Busang gold find in Indonesia, sources close to the talks said on Friday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "The negotiations will be held both in Toronto and in Jakarta," one source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Another source said most of the key negotiators from both Bre-X and Barrick had returned to Toronto, but declined to say if there had been any progress in their negotiations. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Both sources said Bre-X and Barrick did not hold talks on Thursday with Mines and Energy Ministry Secretary-General Umar Said, who is coordinating the negotiations over the Busang find in East Kalimantan. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The first source also said Bre-X had until December 21 to submit to the Indonesian Mines and Energy Ministry a feasibility study on the central region of the Busang property, estimated to contain 2.6 million ounces of gold. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The richest parts of the property to the north and south of the central region have been estimated by Bre-X to contain 57 million ounces of gold. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "Bre-X is expected to complete the feasibility report by December 16 and submit it to the government before the December 21 deadline," the source said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: He said Bre-X would then formally seek the permission of the Indonesian government to begin construction to develop Busang's central region, which might take up to two years. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The source declined to say if there had been any progress in the talks between Bre-X and Barrick. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "This is a huge project ... Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: we are not selling furniture, and Bre-X has 13,000 shareholders to answer to, "the source said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "While there has been some agreement in principle on some issues, there are still others such as procedures and mechanisms that needed to be sorted out," he added. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The source said no new deadline had been set by the Mines and Energy Ministry for Bre-X and Barrick to strike a deal. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The Ministry had given the companies until December 4 to complete a partnership deal, and advised Bre-X to take a 25 percent stake and Barrick 75 percent to develop the property. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "As far as I am aware, there's been no new deadline," the source said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The Ministry's Umar said on Thursday that both Bre-X and Barrick had responded positively to a government letter recommending a 25-75 split in the Busang gold property. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The government also wants 10 percent of the property. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Umar said the government had yet to receive a formal reply from the companies. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: He had said earlier that if the two companies failed to reach a partnership agreement, the government would explore other ways to expedite development of the Busang find. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Bre-X has a partnership deal with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, under which Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake Busang's richest parts. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project". Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: FEATURE - Singapore sees prestige in hosting WTO. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Ramthan Hussain Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: SINGAPORE 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Singapore's winning campaign to host the World Trade Organisation (WTO)'s first ministerial meeting reflected its ambition to play a key role in shaping global free trade, the lifeblood of its economy, analysts said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "As one of the world's most externally oriented economies, Singapore has a disproportionately large stake in the WTO," said Desmond Supple, economist at research house I.D.E.A. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "Singapore stands to benefit more than most from continued global trade liberalisation as trade is the engine of its growth, accounting for nearly three times its gross domestic product." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The city-state met U.S. opposition two years ago in its bid to host the meeting, expected to gather 4,000 officials from 160 countries from December 9 to 13. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: In a stand some analysts linked to controversy over Singapore's caning of an American teenager for vandalism, then-U.S. Trade Representative Mickey Kantor had said the meeting ought to be held where the WTO was going to be headquartered. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: That would have meant Geneva. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But Singapore had the support of other WTO members. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Derek da Cunha, senior fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies (ISEAS), said Singapore's hosting of the conference "carries a great deal of symbolism for the city-state, underscoring its commitment to free trade and its trading links across the globe." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: There is the international prestige Singapore would enjoy, but "more importantly there is a genuine national interest in fostering better global free trade and an open market", said Tan Kong Yam, head of Business Policy at the National University of Singapore. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: At the ministerial meeting, trade ministers will review the work of the WTO and the implementation of the Uruguay Round free trade commitments under its predecessor the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: In June, the WTO hailed Singapore for its open market policies but the European Union and other trading powers called on Singapore to speed up the opening of its services sector. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Supple said the struggle that Singapore had to wage in vying to host the meeting would be repeated during the talks. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "There is tension at every step of the way," since a battle line between the West and developing countries has been drawn over the issue of linking trade liberalisation with labour rights, he said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Supple said hosting the meeting carried prestige for Singapore, "however, this is quite intangible as the prestige factor may not necessarily lead to any additional investment and trade flows to this region." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: From a commercial point of view, the meeting would be good for Singapore's tourism industry, Tan said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: A large part of Singapore's workforce would be mobilised to ensure the meeting would run without a glitch but the average Singaporean "would probably not be too concerned about some of the issues," Tan said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "But the more educated public will realise that these kind of things are important for Singapore as a small economy." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Supple said any political gains the Singapore government would get from the WTO meeting -- ahead of a general election due by April 1997 -- would depend on how successful it was in pushing its economic agenda. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "If there are any movements toward freer trade, then Singapore's economy and the electorate would gain," he said. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But I don't think it would be wise to play up the political aspect of this. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: I think political issues will take secondary importance to all these economic issues that will be displayed. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Japan NTT says hopes to start int'l business soon. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: TOKYO 1996-12-06 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Friday that it hopes to move into the international telecommunications business as soon as possible following the government's decision to split NTT into three firms under a holding company. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "We hope to start international telephone business as soon as possible," a company official told Reuters. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The official said the latest government decision to split the company under a holding company would allow flexibility in NTT's international phone business. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Earlier, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Hisao Horinouchi told a news conference the government plans to split NTT into three firms under a holding company, but did not specify when the restructuring would likely take effect. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: One of the three new companies will be a long-distance operator and the other two will be local-call operators, Horinouchi said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: One of the local firms will operate in west Japan and the other in east Japan, he added. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The long-distance operator will offer international services, Horinouchi said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: The NTT official said the timing of the planned split-up was uncertain because more discussions by government officials were required. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: BOBSLEIGH-SHIMER PILOTS USA III TO SURPRISE WIN. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: IGLS, Austria 1996-12-07 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Brian Shimer piloted USA III to a surprise victory in a World Cup two-man bobsleigh race on Saturday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Lying fifth after the first run, Shimer and breakman Randy Jones delivered a near-perfect second trip down the 1976 Olympic course for an aggregate time of one minute 45.91 seconds. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: First run leaders Guenther Huber and breakman Antonio Tartaglia in the Italy I sleigh finished second two-hundredths of a second behind the Americans. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Canada I, represented by Pierre Lueders and breakman Dave MacEachern, completed the third World cup event of the winter a further one-hundredth of a second behind the Italians. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The Canadians, winners of the opening two events in Altenberg, Germany, and La Plagne, France, increased their lead in the World Cup standings. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: They have 104 points, 15 ahead of USA I's Jim Herberich and breakman Garrett Hines who managed only 10th place on Saturday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: SKIING-CHINESE MAKE PROMISING FREESTYLE SKIING DEBUT. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: TIGNES, France 1996-12-07 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: China made a promising debut on the freestyle skiing world cup circuit in an aerials event in the French resort of Tignes on Saturday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: While the Chinese failed to gain a place in the men's final, they had two in the top 10 of the women's competition, Cuo Dan finishing a respectable seventh and Xu Nannan ninth. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But overall, it was France and Canada who dominated the day. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Alexis Blanc and Sebastien Foucras gave France a one-two finish in the first aerials competition of the season. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Blanc collected his seventh career World Cup win with a two jump combined score of 238.36 points, easily beating Foucras, the overall World Cup aerials champion, who was a distant second with 223.60. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Canada's Jeff Bean, who had never finished higher than ninth in a World Cup event, made his first trip to the podium taking third place with a mark of 209.96. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Veronica Brenner of Canada, who picked up her first career victory at Tignes last year, made it two wins in a row at the French resort taking first in the women's competition with a score of 170.42. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Swiss skiers occupied the other two places on the podium, Karin Kuster taking second with 160.55 narrowly ahead of Evelyne Leu with 160.36. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: CRICKET - WOOLMER MAKES SENTIMENTAL RETURN TO KANPUR. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: KANPUR, India 1996-12-07 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: South Africa's trip to Kanpur for the third test against India has given former England test cricketer Bob Woolmer the chance of a sentimental return to his birthplace. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Woolmer was born in the northern city of Kanpur when his father worked there for an insurance compnay and was himself an active cricketer. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "It's been a sentimental journey ... Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: A visit to India is always an intriguing experience, "Woolmer, now the South African coach, said on Saturday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Woolmer, 48, played 19 tests for England between 1975 and 1981. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: His first cricketing sojurn to India was as a member of Tony Greig's England side in 1976-77. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: His father Clarence Woolmer represented United Province, now renamed Uttar Pradesh, in India's Ranji Trophy national championship and captained the state during 1949. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Now aged 86, Woolmer senior lives with his son in Cape Town. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Woolmer's memories of Kanpur are few and blurred. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "I don't remember much of the place," he said. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: I came here on zero and left at three (aged three) when my father was transferred to Calcutta where I spent another four and half years. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "But I do remember we had a cobra snake in the basement of our house. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Also that my father bought a bicycle and when we rode over a hose pipe it broke into two. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Woolmer said the hospital where he was born is close to the stadium where the India-South Africa test will be played. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
